rows.annotation: Erythromycin esterase-like family hydrolase, substrate specificity undetermined.
rows.evidence: Query PFAM and CDD hits identify the erythromycin esterase family, supported by PIRSF UCP036794 and STRING COG2312. Homologs at 42.3–47.8% identity carry matching annotations, but none provides direct biochemical characterization. The Fitness Browser hit supplies a locus description without condition-specific fitness measurements; neighborhood and STRING associations do not establish substrate specificity.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier B: named enzyme-family domains and homolog annotations support a family-level assignment, but no characterized homolog or substrate-specific fitness data establishes Tier A. Available evidence includes comparative and incidental literature summaries, query domains, homolog domains, neighborhoods, STRING associations, and predicted cytoplasmic topology; fitness and cofitness measurements are absent. A specific erythromycin-hydrolyzing activity or antibiotic-resistance role is not assigned because repeated family annotations do not demonstrate either function.

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 13 (in 9 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 12 (8 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 39.3-100.0
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
